# 328_R7UX.5 — pricing teaser: honest single-anchor copy (BL-96)

Stacked on `stevenvitali/r7ux-4-dossier-visual-unify` (unmerged; mergePolicy OPERATOR).

## Summary

BL-96 (R5 H5, P2): the landing's pricing teaser quoted a credit range
(`2,600 – 11,730 credits`, a 4.5× Base→Frontier span) right next to a run sheet
that quotes a single dollars-first figure (`≈ $85.35 · never more than …`) — the
two figures told different stories. This ticket fixes the *presentation* only:
the teaser now quotes what a review actually costs in the reader's terms — the
estimator's own per-review figure at the anchor the entitlement config exposes,
dollarized the run-sheet way (REQ-BILL-1), with the credit mechanism still
visible.

Rendered line: `5,000 words · 20 claims — a Standard Review on Base costs ≈ $26.10 (2,610 credits)`

## What changed

- `apps/web/src/copy.ts` — new `COPY.landing.pricing.teaserReviewFmt` template
  (`{words}/{claims}/{rigor}/{tier}/{usd}/{credits}` slots, no literal figure), so
  `collectCopyStrings` picks the line up and `lintCopy`/`lintGrowthCopy` cover it.
- `apps/web/src/marketing.tsx` — the `data-section="pricing"` teaser: the pricer
  is hoisted (`surfacePricer()` — the same estimator-facing API as before,
  EST.1/ADR-034), and the figure is `reviewCardCredits(pricer, essayCard…,
  data.trial.entitlement.modelTier)` — the trial entitlement's own rigor
  (`standard`) and tier (`base`) — rendered through the new template via
  `formatUsd`/`formatCredits` + `RIGOR_DISPLAY`/`MODEL_TIER_DISPLAY`. `null`
  renders `—` (the page's fail-closed convention). The 4.5× ` – ` span stays
  where it belongs: `/pricing`'s per-tier cost cards.
- `apps/web/src/marketing.test.ts` — the teaser test now recomputes the anchor
  from the estimator + entitlement config and asserts the derived dollar and
  credit figures, the named rigor+tier, and the absence of any `\d – \d` range
  inside the teaser section.

## Design decisions

- **Anchor = the trial entitlement's own terms** (`PRICING.trial.entitlement`
  = `review · standard · base`, the reader's first-run terms) — the "whichever
  source the entitlement config exposes" branch of the ticket. Named explicitly
  in the copy ("a Standard Review on Base costs …") so a tier that moves the
  figure is never hidden; consistent with the page's existing Base anchors
  (`pricingFaq`'s `reviewBase`, `quickReviewLine`).
- **Dollars lead** (REQ-BILL-1 — the run-sheet register); credits stay visible in
  parens (the ticket's "must not hide the credit mechanism").
- No economics touched: no pricing-model change (BL-13/BL-101), no entitlement
  math, the run sheet and `/pricing` cost cards untouched.
